title: Korean Turkey Rice Bowls
seoTitle: Korean Turkey Rice Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Sweet-spicy turkey with rice and quick pickles
subtitle: Sweet-spicy turkey with rice and quick pickles
description: Turkey is simmered in a garlicky Korean-style sauce with rice, cucumber, and carrots.

steps.title: Cook rice
steps.instruction: Cook rice in lightly salted water and keep it covered after the heat is off.

steps.title: Mix glaze
steps.instruction: Whisk gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, and water until smooth.

steps.title: Quick-pickle cucumber
steps.instruction: Toss sliced cucumber with vinegar, sugar, and salt, then chill while turkey cooks.

steps.title: Heat skillet
steps.instruction: Heat a wide skillet over medium-high and add oil before the turkey.

steps.title: Brown turkey
steps.instruction: Break turkey into fine pieces and cook until all pink colour is gone.

steps.title: Verify turkey
steps.instruction: Check the centre of several pieces; ground turkey must reach 165°F.

steps.title: Glaze meat
steps.instruction: Pour in glaze and simmer until it coats the turkey instead of pooling in the pan.

steps.title: Prep carrots
steps.instruction: Julienne carrots or use matchsticks, keeping them raw for crunch.

steps.title: Hold hot base
steps.instruction: Cover turkey and rice and keep both above 140°F during a delayed meal break.

steps.title: Serve bowls
steps.instruction: Layer rice, turkey, cucumber pickles, carrots, and green onions in each bowl.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Ground turkey — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Ground turkey and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Use mild gochujang for a mixed crew.
Add water if glaze becomes sticky.
Fried eggs make a hearty add-on.
tonightSpread: Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Ground turkey in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Use cold leftovers in lunch lettuce cups.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Fast-cooking ground meat makes this easy to pause and restart around calls.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: mix sauce and pickle cucumbers 2 days ahead. Storage: refrigerate for 3 days. Reheating: heat turkey to 165°F.
